children.raw_text: 62. For the purposes of this Act, the expression "the money supply" means all currency, demand deposits, time and savings deposits and such other financial assets as may be prescribed by the Monetary Board from time to time and are owned by persons other than the Government, Commercial banks and such financial institutions as may be prescribed by the Monetary Board and for the purposes of this section "Financial institutions" shall have the same meaning assigned to it in subsection (5) of section 93,".

body.heading: Replacement of heading in part VI of the principal enactment.
body.raw_text: 19. The heading appearing in part VI immediately before section 93 of the principal enactment is hereby repealed and the following heading substituted therefor:-
body.text: The heading appearing in part VI immediately before section 93 of the principal enactment is hereby repealed and the following heading substituted therefor:-

body.heading: "REGULATION OF THE RESERVES OF COMMERCIAL BANKS AND PRESCRIBED FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS".

children.heading: Replacement of section 93 of the principal enactment.
children.raw_text: 20. Section 93 of the principal enactment is hereby repealed and the following section substituted therefor:- 'Reserve requirements.
children.text: Section 93 of the principal enactment is hereby repealed and the following section substituted therefor:- 'Reserve requirements.

children.raw_text: (1) The Monetary Board shall, in order to limit the volume of money created by the credit operation of the financial system, require commercial banks and such other financial institutions operating in Sri Lanka as may be prescribed by the Monetary Board (in this part referred to as the "prescribed financial institutions") to maintain reserves against their deposit liabilities and such of their other financial liabilities as the Monetary Board may consider necessary and shall, for that purpose, prescribe the classes of deposit liabilities and the categories of other financial liabilities against which reserves are required to be maintained.
children.text: The Monetary Board shall, in order to limit the volume of money created by the credit operation of the financial system, require commercial banks and such other financial institutions operating in Sri Lanka as may be prescribed by the Monetary Board (in this part referred to as the "prescribed financial institutions") to maintain reserves against their deposit liabilities and such of their other financial liabilities as the Monetary Board may consider necessary and shall, for that purpose, prescribe the classes of deposit liabilities and the categories of other financial liabilities against which reserves are required to be maintained.

children.raw_text: (2) The reserves required to be maintained by a commercial bank, or a prescribed financial institution under subsection (1), shall be proportionate to the volumes respectively, of each class of its deposit liabilities and each class of its deposit liabilities and each shall, subject to subsection (4), take the form of rupee deposits in the Central Bank.
children.text: The reserves required to be maintained by a commercial bank, or a prescribed financial institution under subsection (1), shall be proportionate to the volumes respectively, of each class of its deposit liabilities and each class of its deposit liabilities and each shall, subject to subsection (4), take the form of rupee deposits in the Central Bank.

children.raw_text: (3) The accounts maintained at the Central Bank by prescribed financial institutions under subsection (2), shall be maintained only for the purpose of keeping the rupee deposits required to be maintained as reserves by such financial institutions.
children.text: The accounts maintained at the Central Bank by prescribed financial institutions under subsection (2), shall be maintained only for the purpose of keeping the rupee deposits required to be maintained as reserves by such financial institutions.

children.raw_text: (4) The Monetary Board may in the interest of the national economy and the banking and financial systems of the country, permit the maintenance of any part of the reserves required to be maintained under subsection (1), in the form of assets other than rupee deposits in the Central Bank.

children.raw_text: "Financial business" in relation to a financial institution means the accepting of money in any form from the public, in the ordinary course of business, by way of deposit or by the issue of bills of exchange, promissory notes, bonds, certificates, notes, commercial paper of other similar instruments by means of which money is raised from the public, and the use of that money, in whole or in part, for the grant of loans or making that money available to third parties or for the benefit of third parties, as a business;

children.raw_text: "Financial institution" means a licensed specialised bank as defined in the Banking Act, No. 30 of 1988 or a finance company as defined in the finance Companies Act. No. 78 of 1988, and includes any person or body of persons carrying on financial business ;
